brief: A global bond rout last week triggered record dip-buying: US bond futures logged their largest weekly net buying in JPM's 5-year history ($89bn, 3.4z), fully reversing the prior week's selling, and US-listed fixed income ETFs drew a record $29.6bn (3.7z), led by Municipals, Government Bonds (long-term Treasuries) and Money Market, while Mortgages saw outflows and credit flows were mixed. In equities, investors de-risked Semis (Tech ETFs -$3.7bn, SOXL/SOXX/SMH -$4.0bn combined) while buying option-based strategies and levered single-stock ETFs tracking AMD, Intel and SanDisk; a model rebalance rotated sector allocations from Financials into Utilities. CFTC data showed Asset Managers sold SPX and Leveraged Funds sold EAFE/MID futures, and Managed Money broadly sold commodity futures, led by Natural Gas, Silver and WTI, even as CTAs stayed net long equities (ex-EMEA) and incrementally sold Metals. Bond futures liquidity deteriorated sharply during the sell-off, with US and EMEA market depth several standard deviations below average.
